newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A index closes firmer, B trading closed.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A index closes firmer, B trading closed.

text.p: Shenzhen's A shares extended Monday morning's gains on an optimistic outlook for China's economy while the B share market remained closed in line with Hong Kong's Easter holiday.
The domestic currency A index added 11.74 points or 2.63 percent to close at 458.49 points. Turnover was 10.8 billion yuan against Friday's 10.5 billion yuan.
"Good words on the economy perked up market sentiment," a trader at Central-South Securities said.
China's State Statistical Bureau said China's economy would grow by 10 percent in 1997 with inflation around five percent, according to Monday's Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
Traders said the absence of a market clampdown widely rumoured last week also buoyed market mood.
"The absence of regulatory news contributed to today's gains," an analyst at Xiangcai Securities said.
Shenzhen's B share market has been closed since Friday. Trading will resume on Tuesday morning.
However, the exchange system indicated that 224,000 B shares worth HK$1.1 million were traded on Friday morning, pushing the index up 0.42 points to 162.56 points.
Friday's transactions would be carried over to Tuesday, an exchange statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said.
"Because of technical reasons, the B share trade on March 28 is effective, and will be included in the next trading day," the statement said but gave no details.
